title: Are you passing along something true or false? Dissemination of social media messages about genetically modified organisms
screen_reason: The study's aim is network dissemination, but the content-coding stage reports how many of the 482 most-reposted GMO posts on Sina Weibo in 2018 were coded as misinformation (161), true (137) and unknown (184), giving a CONTENT share with a stated denominator. The dissemination results themselves are network metrics (density, modularity, transitivity, repost counts), not prevalence shares.

estimates.measure_type: % of the 482 most-reposted Chinese-language GMO posts on Weibo coded as containing misinformation
estimates.value_raw: 161/482 posts coded as verifiable misinformation (137 true, 184 unknown)
estimates.denominator: 482 original Weibo posts: the 500 most-reposted of 68,237 posts matching the keyword zhuan ji yin (GMO) in 2018, minus 18 that used the keyword without discussing GMOs
estimates.definition: post contained verifiably false, incorrect or misleading statement(s) about GMOs, regardless of intent; posts mixing true and false content were coded as misinformation unless the false content was quoted for a valid correction
estimates.misinfo_def: we define misinformation as false or misleading information regardless of intention for sharing. Following this conceptualization, fake news, satire, rumor, and any imposter, manipulated, or fabricated content are all considered as misinformation
estimates.source_quote: The content coding identified 137 posts with verifiably true information and 161 posts with verifiable misinformation about GMOs, with 184 posts as unknown.
estimates.page_loc: Sample for content coding (p. 6) and Sample for constructing dissemination networks (p. 9)
estimates.ground_truth_detail: Two researchers with GMO research experience and Mandarin as first language, trained, pilot-coded 50 posts to consensus, then double-coded 100 posts (20.7% of the sample): Krippendorff's alpha = .82 for information veracity, 1.0 for account verification; one researcher coded the remainder. Veracity was cross-checked against five Chinese fact-checking services (Rumor Smasher/Guokr, Songshuhui, WeChat Rumor Filter, Tencent Jiaozhen, Toutiao Piyao) and six expert bodies (Chinese Ministry of Agriculture, Chinese Academy of Sciences, WHO, US National Academy of Sciences, EFSA, US EPA), against scientific consensus at the time of coding.
estimates.moderator_quote: A total of 68,237 original Chinese posts containing the keyword of zhuan ji yin were collected. We ranked all these original posts by number of received reposts and selected the top 500 posts. ... When verifying the falsity and validity of information, we have used the following leading fact-checking online services in Chinese
estimates.notes: Value derived per R8 as an exact part/whole share from verbatim counts with the same denominator (161/482 = 33.4%); no percentage is printed in the paper. denom_selection = curated because the sample is the top 500 by repost count, so it over-represents highly shared posts and is not a random sample of GMO discourse. GROUND-TRUTH JUDGEMENT CALL: coded researcher_coding rather than fact_checker because the two trained researchers made the veracity determinations themselves (the Table 1 rationales are their own reasoning against primary scientific sources), with fact-checking services used as one verification input among several; an adjudicator preferring 'external ground truth was a fact-check verdict' could defensibly code fact_checker. breadth = misleading because the definition explicitly covers true statements used misleadingly. Source quote replaced (it was an ellipsis join of two sentences from different sections) with the single sentence carrying the numerator; quote_verbatim=false because the rendering breaks "verifiable" across a line as "verifi-" / "able", so the sentence is faithful but not byte-identical to the file. The denominator sentence, in the preceding section, reads: "These 18 posts were excluded from the subsequent coding, which resulted in a sample of 482 original posts for content coding." 161/482 = 33.4%.

missed_or_uncertain: (1) 137/482 true (28.4%) and 184/482 unknown (38.2%) are not misinformation shares. (2) A stricter share, misinformation as a proportion of verifiable posts only (161 of 137+161 = 54.0%), was NOT extracted: 298 is a cross-category sum I would have had to compute, which R8 forbids. An adjudicator should know it exists, because the 33.4% figure counts the 38% unverifiable posts in its denominator and so is not comparable to studies that drop unverifiable items. (3) The 200-post network sample splits 132 verified (66%) / 68 unverified (34%) accounts, which is a source-attribute share, not a misinformation share. (4) All dissemination results are network metrics with means (reposts M = 760.93, reach M = 568.43, density, modularity, transitivity) and F tests, with no share of reposts or users carrying misinformation, so no SHARING or REACH row is derivable: the 100 misinformation and 100 true posts were selected in equal numbers by design, which makes any repost split an artefact of the sampling, not an estimate.

rob.design: Keyword census of publicly available Sina Weibo posts for 'zhuan ji yin' across all of 2018 (68,237 original posts) collected by Python scraping of search result pages, then rank-truncated to the top 500 by repost count and reduced to 482 on-topic posts. Veracity coded by two trained bilingual researchers into misinformation / true / unknown, cross-checked against five Chinese fact-checking services and six scientific bodies; reliability established on 100 double-coded posts (Krippendorff's alpha = .82 for veracity, 1.0 for account verification), remainder single-coded. Main limitations for a prevalence estimate: the denominator is the most-reposted tail, not a random sample; only publicly available posts and retrievable reposts were captured; 38% of posts were unverifiable and kept in the denominator; one platform, one country, one topic.
rob.item6_quote: The post with misinformation about GMOs was operationalized as the one containing verifiably false, incorrect, or misleading statement(s) about GMOs, regardless of whether the post was intentionally false/misleading or not.
rob.item10_quote: The content coding identified 137 posts with verifiably true information and 161 posts with verifiable misinformation about GMOs, with 184 posts as unknown.
